o:
Simply validate six conditions: length ≥ 8, at least one lowercase, one uppercase, one digit, one special from '!@#$%^&*()-+', and no two identical adjacent characters.

'IloveLe3tcode!' passes all. 'Me+You--IsMyDream' fails: no digit and the '--' adjacency. '1aB!' fails on length.

Length ≤ 100 means a single linear scan suffices.
k: Track boolean flags for each character-class requirement during one pass.
Check the adjacency violation inline: password[i] == password[i-1] fails immediately.

a.i: Iterate once, setting flags for lowercase/uppercase/digit/special, failing fast on adjacent duplicates, then AND the flags with the length check.
s: Scan characters: set class flags; reject if current char equals previous.
Return conjunction of all four class flags.
a.t: O(n) — one pass over the password.

w: Trivial validation problem; the pitfalls are the exact special-character set (note '-' and '+' are included) and checking adjacency before/after flags doesn't matter but early exit on duplicates saves nothing important. Follow-up: LeetCode 420 (Strong Password Checker) adds insertion/deletion/replacement minimization — much harder.
